name: English Wikipedia
licence: CC BY-SA; reuse permitted with attribution
access: MediaWiki API, descriptive User-Agent with contact, serial ~1/second, cached on first fetch

RANK.position: BELOW media guides and contemporary newspapers
RANK.why: user-edited, and its infobox fields are effectively uncited -- birth date 0%, college 0%, draft 0%, and only 6.7% of infoboxes (23 of 344) carry a reference anywhere.
RANK.uncited_is_not_unused: for most of these men it is the only source for death date, high school and draft. It is attributed and ranked, not excluded.

DISAGREEMENTS_ARE_HELD: Never resolved. Where Wikipedia and StatsCrew differ, BOTH values stay, both attributed. The archive says what is known and says who says it.

IDENTITY.pre_1950: the article must NAME THE CLUB. A year match is never sufficient -- any football article about anybody mentions years.
IDENTITY.from_1950: club name, or year plus football context.
IDENTITY.insufficient: UNMATCHED. No claims at all, not a partial attachment.
IDENTITY._measured: 0 of 835 pre-1950 club-seasons hold two distinct people with the same name, so club+year discriminates within our universe and POSITION IS UNNECESSARY. The risk is a namesake OUTSIDE our universe, which is why the article must name the club.
IDENTITY._DEFECT_FOUND_AND_FIXED: the club map is keyed {club_code}|{year}. Four earlier probes looked it up as {league}|{year}|{code}, which returns None for every club, so the club branch never fired and every 'confirmed on club and era' was era-only. Corrected before any ingest.

PHOTOGRAPHS.rule: GAP-FILL ONLY. Never overwrite a photograph already held.
PHOTOGRAPHS.licence: PUBLIC DOMAIN or OPEN CC. Fair use is EXCLUDED.
PHOTOGRAPHS._why_not_PD_alone: all seven CFL images measured were open CC and none were public domain, so a PD-only filter would silently drop the CFL entirely.
PHOTOGRAPHS._verified_keys: lives in the GAME roster files under tools/, not in this store. This ingest writes only dataset/build/wikipedia.json and touches no game file.

PROSE.capture_the_citation: a cited prose claim and an uncited one must be distinguishable in the store. 48.2% of narrative sentences carry an inline citation.
PROSE.reference_list: recorded independently of the claims. 1,012 newspaper citations across 344 articles is a map of documents that exist, built by people who already did the finding.

hard_rules: no claim without a source attribution
no photograph overwrites one already held
a fair-use image cannot be expressed, not merely forbidden
an unmatched person produces no claims at all
a prose claim records whether it is cited, queryably

_documentation_only._rule: keys addressed to a reader and to no code path. Everything NOT listed here must be read by something in src/ -- see src/gate_declarations_are_read.py.
_documentation_only.licence: the reuse terms of the source itself, a rights note
_documentation_only.access: how it was fetched; the politeness contract, not a code path
_documentation_only.RANK: where this source sits against guides and newspapers. Ranking is applied at resolution, not at ingest, so nothing here reads it yet.
_documentation_only.DISAGREEMENTS_ARE_HELD: a statement of policy; the ENFORCEMENT is that ingest_wikipedia never resolves, and gate_wikipedia proves both values survive
_documentation_only.PROSE: free prose about why citations travel with claims; the enforcement is the required `cited` field
